newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate moderates rise on peso.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate moderates rise on peso.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates closed up 90 basis points at 17.40 percent on Wednesday.
Dealers said rates earlier had risen as high as 18.00 percent in an adjustment from a late dip the day before, but gains were pared on foreign demand and a strong peso.

"Foreign investors have done their homework... Greenspan confirmed the U.S. economy was on course, then domestic rates have been able to decline and the peso has firmed up," a fixed-income analyst said, referring to congressional testimony by U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan.
Benchmark 48-hour Cetes rates closed 0.8 of a centavo firmer at 7.8280/7.8330 per dollar.
Dealers noted that Banco de Mexico drained 640 million pesos from the market, a much-smaller amount than in many recent sessions.
Overnight rates on bank paper ended up 50 basis points at 18.85 percent.
Liquidity of 1.807 billion pesos was scheduled to return to the system from prior central bank participation.
